title: The Late Portrait
premise: Estate lawyer Lena Eriksen is handed a will naming a woman, Astrid Voss, who vanished thirty years ago and was declared dead—yet the will is dated two years after her disappearance. Worse, the diary found with it continues past the date Astrid was last seen, written in a hand that grows shakier but never stops. As Lena traces the beneficiaries—a lighthouse keeper's son, a disgraced nun, and a man who changed his name twice—she uncovers a survival pact gone wrong: Astrid faked her death to escape a violent husband, then lived hidden among the very people who helped her vanish. The diary's final entries reveal that Astrid died only recently, and that one of her protectors has been quietly killing anyone who came close to finding her. In the climax, Lena confronts the killer at the derelict coastal cottage where Astrid spent her last years, surviving an attack long enough for the truth—and Astrid's real final letter—to surface. The novel ends with the estate finally settled: Astrid's money goes to the daughter she never stopped watching from afar, and Lena, who lost her own family young, accepts that the people we choose can inherit us.
about_author: Tamsin Amberdale spent a decade working in probate offices along the Norwegian-Scottish coast before turning to fiction full-time. She writes mysteries about paperwork, secrets, and the quiet violence hidden inside ordinary legal documents.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Lena Eriksen opens a probate file containing a will dated 1997—two years after Astrid Voss disappeared and was declared dead. Her senior partner urges her to reject it as fraud, but the notarization is flawless. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into fascination.

chapters.title: Paper Ghost
chapters.summary: Lena pulls the original missing-persons file: Astrid Voss, 34, vanished from the fishing town of Skerrow in 1994, presumed drowned. No body. The will names three beneficiaries she's never heard of. POV: Lena. Beat: the first crack—the dead don't usually sign things.

chapters.title: The Diary in the Evidence Box
chapters.summary: A solicitor in Skerrow sends Astrid's recovered effects, including a diary. Its last entry is dated 2001—seven years after her disappearance. Lena reads the first pages: fear, planning, a woman rehearsing her own death. POV: Lena. Beat: dread mixed with intimacy.

chapters.title: Beneficiary One: The Keeper's Son
chapters.summary: Lena travels to Skerrow and finds Ewan Marris, now a boat mechanic, named in the will. He goes pale at Astrid's name and slams the door—but not before she sees a photograph of the old lighthouse on his wall. POV: Lena. Beat: hostility that reads like guilt.

chapters.title: Beneficiary Two: Sister Ruth
chapters.summary: In a coastal convent, former nun Ruth Calloway receives Lena cautiously. She admits knowing Astrid 'in another life' and offers nothing else, but her hands shake when the diary is mentioned. POV: Lena. Beat: piety as armor.

chapters.title: Beneficiary Three: The Man Twice Renamed
chapters.summary: The third beneficiary, Daniel Ostrick, died last year. His obituary lists a prior name: Anders Voss—Astrid's husband, the man she fled. Lena realizes the will leaves money to the man she ran from. POV: Lena. Beat: the case tilts from strange to sinister.

chapters.title: Entries Before the Water
chapters.summary: Back home, Lena reads the diary's early months: bruises described in flat, clinical language, then a plan taking shape involving a boat, a coat left on rocks, and someone called only 'the Keeper.' POV: alternating diary/Lena. Beat: horror in bureaucratic calm.

chapters.title: The Statute Clock
chapters.summary: Lena learns the estate cannot be settled until the death date is legally established—and if Astrid died recently, certain claims expire within months. A rival firm begins sniffing around the file. POV: Lena. Beat: time pressure introduced.

chapters.title: What Ewan Won't Say
chapters.summary: Lena corners Ewan at his workshop. He admits he was sixteen in 1994 and saw Astrid the night she vanished—alive, rowing toward the lighthouse—but swore an oath of silence to his father, the keeper. POV: Ewan flashback framed by Lena. Beat: loyalty versus conscience.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Log
chapters.summary: The decommissioned lighthouse still holds its logbooks. The final 1994 entries show extra supplies drawn, a second bed made up, and then a page torn out. Someone erased the evidence of shelter. POV: Lena. Beat: discovery shadowed by deliberate erasure.

chapters.title: Sister Ruth's Confession, Part One
chapters.summary: Ruth admits she helped Astrid reach a women's refuge in 1994, believing the story of a drowning husband—not a faked drowning wife. She says Astrid wrote to her for years, then stopped abruptly in 2003. POV: Ruth. Beat: guilt of the deceived helper.

chapters.title: A Daughter in the File
chapters.summary: Digging into Astrid's history, Lena finds a child: Maren Voss, born 1988, raised by an aunt after the disappearance, told her mother abandoned her. She's a nurse in Inverness and wants nothing to do with any of it. POV: Lena. Beat: the human cost surfaces.

chapters.title: Maren Refuses
chapters.summary: Lena meets Maren, who is bitter and closed: her mother chose to disappear; let her stay gone. But when Lena mentions the diary continuing past 1994, something flickers—Maren asks, too quickly, how far past. POV: Maren. Beat: anger hiding hunger.

chapters.title: The Handwriting Question
chapters.summary: A forensic document examiner confirms the post-1994 diary entries are Astrid's writing, degraded over years by illness or age. The will's signature matches too. Astrid lived—and signed—long after her death. POV: Lena. Beat: the impossible becomes documented fact.

chapters.title: Who Knew, Who Told
chapters.summary: Lena maps the circle: keeper, nun, refuge worker, and one unnamed name recurring in the diary as 'H.' Whoever H was handled Astrid's money, mail, and medicine. POV: Lena. Beat: the shape of a conspiracy emerges.

chapters.title: First Threat
chapters.summary: Lena's office is broken into overnight; only the Voss file is disturbed, and the diary is nearly taken. A note in her car: 'Some estates settle themselves.' POV: Lena. Beat: fear arrives personally.

chapters.title: Ewan Breaks
chapters.summary: After the break-in, Ewan comes to Lena voluntarily. His father didn't just shelter Astrid—he took payment for it, monthly, from a man he never named. The payments stopped in 2003, the year the letters stopped. POV: Ewan. Beat: betrayal inside the sanctuary.

chapters.title: Following the Money
chapters.summary: Lena traces the payments through a shell charity to Daniel Ostrick/Anders Voss. The husband funded his wife's hiding place—for fifteen years. Why would a hunter pay to keep his prey alive? POV: Lena. Beat: motive inversion.

chapters.title: The Diary Turns Dark
chapters.summary: The 1999–2001 entries change tone: Astrid writes of being watched, of a face at the window, of deciding not to tell even Ruth. The final legible entry: 'If I stop writing, it means H decided.' POV: diary/Lena. Beat: claustrophobic terror.

chapters.title: Ruth's Confession, Part Two
chapters.summary: Pressed, Ruth reveals H: Halvard Brandt, the refuge's quiet benefactor, who moved Astrid between safe houses and controlled everything. He believed he was protecting her—or so he said. He still lives, retired, above the harbor. POV: Ruth. Beat: the protector unmasked.

chapters.title: Halvard Brandt
chapters.summary: Lena interviews Brandt, urbane and grief-stricken, who claims Astrid died peacefully in 2016 of illness and asked him to burn everything. He produces a death certificate—private burial, no inquest. It's almost airtight. Almost. POV: Lena. Beat: meeting the antagonist and half-believing him.

chapters.title: The Grave That Isn't
chapters.summary: Lena locates the private plot: a headstone, but the cemetery's records show no interment fee ever paid. Exhumation requires proof of death she doesn't have. POV: Lena. Beat: institutional walls closing in.

chapters.title: Maren Returns
chapters.summary: Maren appears at Lena's office, having read a leaked news item about the case. She brings something of her own: birthday cards sent anonymously every year until 2015, each postmarked from Skerrow. Her mother watched her all along. POV: Maren. Beat: rage cracking into longing.

chapters.title: Postmark Skerrow
chapters.summary: The cards were mailed from the village shop, whose owner remembers a 'summer visitor'—a thin woman with a scarf, always at dusk, always alone, except once with a tall grey-haired man. Brandt. POV: shopkeeper via Lena. Beat: the hidden life becomes visible.

chapters.title: What the Payments Bought
chapters.summary: Reconstructing accounts, Lena finds Brandt wasn't paying the keeper to hide Astrid from Anders—he was paying to keep Anders away. Anders knew she lived, and Brandt bought silence. Protection or ownership? POV: Lena. Beat: the moral ground shifts.

chapters.title: Anders Ostrick's Papers
chapters.summary: Through the probate of Ostrick's own estate, Lena obtains his papers: photos of Astrid taken years after 1994, surveillance logs, and unsent letters begging forgiveness. He knew. He watched. And he kept paying. POV: Lena. Beat: obsession dressed as remorse.

chapters.title: The Diary's Hidden Leaves
chapters.summary: Document examination reveals pages removed from the diary's binding—recovered microscopically: impressions mention 'the cottage at Vatnscar' and 'the last winter.' A location Brandt never disclosed. POV: Lena. Beat: the map to the end.

chapters.title: Vatnscar
chapters.summary: Lena finds the cottage: remote, abandoned since roughly 2016, furnished for invalid care. In a locked drawer, medicines prescribed by a doctor whose license was revoked in 2017—an off-grid death, unwitnessed. POV: Lena. Beat: standing inside a stranger's final years.

chapters.title: The Unwitnessed Death
chapters.summary: The struck-off doctor, tracked down, admits signing a private certificate under pressure from Brandt, never seeing the body. Legally, Astrid Voss may have no death at all. POV: doctor via Lena. Beat: the machinery of concealment exposed.

chapters.title: Brandt Realizes
chapters.summary: Brandt calls Lena, voice changed: he knows what she's found. He offers her the estate's executorship and a generous fee to declare 2016 and seal the file. She declines. That night her tires are slashed. POV: Lena. Beat: the mask drops.

chapters.title: Maren's Choice
chapters.summary: Maren, given the diary to read, spends a night with her mother's words—the plans, the guilt, the line 'I watch my daughter from the water's edge.' At dawn she tells Lena: exhume the grave. Whatever's there, she wants the truth. POV: Maren. Beat: reconciliation through resolve.

chapters.title: The Order
chapters.summary: Lena petitions the court using the flawed certificate, the unpaid fees, and the doctor's statement. The exhumation is granted over Brandt's lawyer's furious objections. Date set: ten days out. POV: Lena. Beat: victory that feels like a countdown.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Surveillance photos arrive anonymously at Lena's office—pictures of Lena herself, taken over weeks. The message is clear: stop. Instead she requests police protection and gets a single skeptical constable, Rhona Teague, who starts reading the file. POV: Lena. Beat: isolation deepening, one ally gained.

chapters.title: Rhona Reads
chapters.summary: Constable Teague, hooked by the diary, digs into Brandt's past: a prior ward who died under his 'care' in 1989, ruled accidental. Pattern established. She formally opens an inquiry. POV: Rhona. Beat: institutional power finally tilting toward truth.

chapters.title: Brandt Runs
chapters.summary: Brandt liquidates accounts and disappears; his house holds shredded documents and, in the fireplace ash, corner of a photograph—the cottage at Vatnscar, recent. He's going back to destroy what remains. POV: Rhona/Lena. Beat: the race begins.

chapters.title: The Exhumation
chapters.summary: At the graveside, the coffin is opened: it contains weighted sandbags and Astrid's coat from 1994—the props of the original drowning. Brandt staged a false body to close the story forever. Astrid was never in the ground. POV: Lena. Beat: revelation as vindication and horror.

chapters.title: Vatnscar Again
chapters.summary: Acting on the photo fragment, Lena and Rhona drive through fog to the cottage and find Brandt burning papers in the yard. In the confrontation he confesses: Astrid tried to leave his protection in 2015, to reclaim her daughter; he prevented it, and her health collapsed that winter. He kept her until she died—of a broken heart, he insists. When Lena presses for the truth of the final night, he turns violent. Rhona intervenes; Brandt is arrested. Beat: climax—truth extracted at physical cost.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: Among the salvaged papers is Astrid's true final letter, dictated weakly in 2016: not to Brandt, but to Maren—explaining why she stayed hidden (to keep Anders's violence from finding her daughter), and asking forgiveness for choosing absence over danger. POV: letter/Maren. Beat: catharsis; the mother's voice finally heard.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: The court accepts the reconstructed timeline; the estate settles. Astrid's assets pass to Maren, with bequests to Ewan and Ruth—payment, at last, for their silence and kindness. Brandt awaits trial for the 1989 death and the concealment. Anders's claims die with the statute. POV: Lena. Beat: justice, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: From the Water's Edge
chapters.summary: Months later, Maren scatters flowers at Skerrow's shore while Ewan repairs the lighthouse lamp as a memorial. Lena, invited as family rather than counsel, realizes the case gave her what she'd lost: people who chose her. The diary's last readable line closes the book: 'Being seen was worth everything it cost.' POV: ensemble. Beat: resolution—inheritance as belonging.
